prompt.context: Your client, Critical Transportation (CT), provides logistical support for the rail industry on the West Coast of the United States. Due to the recent Panama Canal expansion, CT is expecting a shift in rail volume to the East Coast once the expanded canal opens in early 2016. CT has retained our firm's services to determine if it should make the investment to expand its business to the East Coast.
prompt.question: Should Critical Transportation expand its business to the East Coast? Determine whether CT's current business model would be profitable on the East Coast, and whether entry into this market makes sense given the shifts in the market.

clarifying_info.q: What is CT's current market position?
clarifying_info.a: CT is a market leader on the West Coast with 25% market share. There are 5 competitors and the total West Coast market size is $2B.

clarifying_info.q: What does CT's business model look like?
clarifying_info.a: CT provides rail transportation services from major port locations on the West Coast to distribution centers all over the Western U.S. Once cargo is loaded (completed by port personnel), they transport via rail to a final location where it is unloaded by their client. CT does not provide any additional services.

clarifying_info.q: What trends are expected in the market?
clarifying_info.a: It is estimated that 25% of West Coast container traffic will shift to the East Coast beginning in 2016. Over time, the West and East Coast ports are expected to equalize in revenue earned per year.

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive landscape on the East Coast?
clarifying_info.a: There are only 3 other comparable companies on the East Coast that focus on CT's core competency, and these companies have no West Coast presence.

clarifying_info.q: What are the expected costs to enter the East Coast market?
clarifying_info.a: CT estimates that entry into the East Coast market will cost a minimum of $450M, but once entered, East Coast operations will cost approximately the same as West Coast operations.

exhibits.title: Initial Market Analysis for 2015 Port Shipping by Rail (East Coast)
exhibits.shows: A table showing three East Coast competitors' market share and total estimated costs, plus a table of total East Coast market revenue from 2011 to 2015.

framework: External: market factors (Panama Canal expansion shifting volume East), customer demand, regulatory concerns
Revenue: pricing strategy, volume, service offerings on East Coast
Costs: identify variable and fixed costs, benchmark against East Coast competitors
Market: competition landscape, market share potential, barriers to entry
Entry mode: acquisition, joint venture, or build from ground up

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1, what should CT's profit margins be in the East Coast market?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate describes the logic before computing. The key insight is that profit margin is consistent regardless of market share tier because cost structure scales proportionally with revenue. Candidate should compute 1 - (total costs / total revenue) for each competitor and note all yield ~20%.

math.setup: Use each competitor's market share and costs relative to total market revenue ($1,000M in 2015) to derive profit margin. Alternatively: 1 - (sum of all costs / total market revenue).
steps: Company A: Revenue = 40% x $1,000M = $400M; Profit = $400M - $320M = $80M; Margin = $80M / $400M = 20%
Company B: Revenue = 35% x $1,000M = $350M; Profit = $350M - $280M = $70M; Margin = $70M / $350M = 20%
Company C: Revenue = 25% x $1,000M = $250M; Profit = $250M - $200M = $50M; Margin = $250M / $250M... wait: $50M / $250M = 20%

questions.prompt: CT can only capture 10% of the East Coast market upon entry in the first year. The West Coast market is $2B and 25% of it is expected to shift East after the canal opens in 2016. The initial investment is $450M. When would CT break even? (Ignore time value of money and assume no growth.)
questions.guidance: A strong candidate projects the East Coast market size after the canal shift, calculates CT's Year 1 revenue and profit, then divides the initial investment by annual profit. The candidate should connect the 2015 data to the 2016 projection and articulate the strategic implication of a 15-year payback.

math.setup: Project East Coast market revenue in 2016 by adding the diverted West Coast traffic. Then compute CT's share, apply 20% margin, and divide $450M investment by annual profit.
steps: 25% of $2,000M West Coast market shifts East = $500M additional revenue
CT captures 10% of $1,500M = $150M in Year 1 revenue

brainstorming.prompt: Given that it would take many years to recoup initial costs unless CT could gain a larger market share, what are some other recommendations for CT to increase profitability on the East Coast after the Panama Canal expansion?

categories.name: Buy / Borrow (Entry Strategy)
ideas: Acquire one of the 3 existing East Coast competitors to immediately gain market share and avoid build costs
Form a joint venture with an East Coast player to share entry costs and leverage local expertise
License CT's operational model to an East Coast partner

categories.name: Expand Service Offerings
ideas: Add value-added logistics services such as repackaging cargo for end vendors
Provide pricing/tag updates for retail clients to capture margin beyond pure rail transport
Offer warehousing or distribution center management adjacent to rail terminals

categories.name: Modal Diversification
ideas: Enter trucking / last-mile delivery as a complement to rail, capturing more of the supply chain
Offer intermodal solutions combining rail and truck to serve distribution centers not near rail lines

categories.name: Customer / Pricing Strategy
ideas: Use existing West Coast client relationships to win East Coast contracts proactively before arrival
Aggressive introductory pricing to capture market share faster and compress the 15-year break-even
Bundle West Coast and East Coast services for national clients to increase switching costs

recommendation: CT should proceed with East Coast expansion given the structural shift in shipping volume driven by the Panama Canal expansion, but must pursue an entry strategy that accelerates market share capture beyond 10% to improve the 15-year break-even horizon

A build-from-scratch entry at 10% share yields a 15-year payback — acceptable only if CT can grow share faster; acquiring an existing East Coast competitor would immediately improve market share and shorten payback
risks: 15-year break-even at 10% market share is long; if CT cannot grow share, capital may be better deployed elsewhere
West Coast revenue will shrink as 25% of volume migrates East, creating a dual pressure on profitability
East Coast incumbents with no West Coast presence may respond aggressively to defend share
Regulatory or infrastructure barriers on the East Coast rail network could increase costs beyond $450M estimate
next_steps: Conduct due diligence on acquiring one of the 3 East Coast competitors to fast-track market share
Model scenarios at 15%, 20%, and 25% market share to determine minimum share needed for acceptable payback
Assess CT's West Coast client base for cross-coast contract opportunities to anchor initial East Coast revenue
Identify value-added service opportunities (repackaging, tagging) that could lift margin above the 20% baseline
